title: Northern Catalpa: Ancient Northern Catalpas You Can Visit
meta_description: The cigar tree, white with flowers in June. Wisconsin's champion is 28 metres tall, and one of its limbs is so heavy it rests on concrete blocks.
intro: In Platteville, Wisconsin, one limb of the state's champion northern catalpa is so heavy that it rests on concrete blocks. The tree stands south of the library on the university campus, 28 metres tall and 6.71 metres round, though the trunk splits so low that the measurers took that figure at 36 inches instead of chest height. Northern catalpa flowers in June in upright clusters of white bells, spotted yellow and purple inside, and then hangs long bean-like pods that stay on through winter, which is why Americans call it the cigar tree. Its natural range is a small patch of the Mississippi basin. Portland put a pair in Irvington on its heritage list in 1994, the year the list opened, at 4.1 and 3.8 metres round. In Ottawa, a third grows on Green Island at the Rideau Falls, among the war memorials, with no measurement on record. None of the three has a published age.
